intro.title: Book Introduction - Philemon
intro.html:
Book Introduction - Philemon

The Epistle of Paul the Apostle to Philemon

WRITER: The Apostle Paul (Phm 1:1)

DATE: Probably A.D. 64. It is one of the Prison Epistles. See Introductions to Ephesians and Colossians.

THEME: Onesimus ("profitable"), a slave of Philemon, a Christian of Colosse, had robbed his master and fled to Rome. There he became a convert through Paul, who sent him back to Philemon with this letter. It is of priceless value as a teaching

(1) in practical righteousness;

(2) in Christian brotherhood;

(3) in Christian courtesy;

(4) in the law of love.

The divisions are four

1. Greeting Phm 1:1-3.

2. The character of Phm 1:4-7.

3. Intercession for Onesimus, Phm 1:8-21.

4. Salutations and conclusion, Phm 1:22-25.

verses.text: Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer,
verses.marked_text: Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer,
verses.outlines: HOW TO USE THE SUBJECT REFERENCES.

verses.text: And to our beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fellowsoldier, and to the church in thy house:
verses.marked_text: And to our beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fellowsoldier, and to the church in thy house:

verses.text: Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.marked_text: Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.text: I thank my God, making mention of thee always in my prayers,
verses.marked_text: I thank my God, making mention of thee always in my prayers,

verses.text: Hearing of thy love and faith, which thou hast toward the Lord Jesus, and toward all saints;
verses.marked_text: Hearing of thy love and faith, which thou hast toward the Lord Jesus, and toward all saints;

verses.text: That the communication of thy faith may become effectual by the acknowledging of every good thing which is in you in Christ Jesus.
verses.marked_text: That the communication of thy faith may become effectual by the acknowledging of every good thing which is in you in Christ Jesus.

verses.text: For we have great joy and consolation in thy love, because the bowels of the saints are refreshed by thee, brother.
verses.marked_text: For we have great joy and consolation in thy love, because the bowels of the saints are refreshed by thee, brother.

verses.text: Wherefore, though I might be much bold in Christ to enjoin thee that which is convenient,
verses.marked_text: Wherefore, though I might be much bold in Christ to enjoin thee that which is convenient,

verses.text: Yet for love’s sake I rather beseech thee, being such an one as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
verses.marked_text: Yet for love’s sake I rather beseech thee, being such an one as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.

verses.text: I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds:
verses.marked_text: I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds:

verses.text: Which in time past was to thee unprofitable, but now profitable to thee and to me:
verses.marked_text: Which in time past was to thee unprofitable, but now profitable to thee and to me:

verses.text: Whom I have sent again: thou therefore receive him, that is, mine own bowels:
verses.marked_text: Whom I have sent again: thou therefore receive him, that is, mine own bowels:

verses.text: Whom I would have retained with me, that in thy stead he might have ministered unto me in the bonds of the gospel:
verses.marked_text: Whom I would have retained with me, that in thy stead he might have ministered unto me in the bonds of the gospel:
verses.outlines: Here Gospel is the subject; vs. 1, 14, 15 show where it is at that particular place; Mk. 8. 35 is the next reference in the chain, and the references in parenthesis are the first and last.

verses.text: But without thy mind would I do nothing; that thy benefit should not be as it were of necessity, but willingly.
verses.marked_text: But without thy mind would I do nothing; that thy benefit should not be as it were of necessity, but willingly.

verses.text: For perhaps he therefore departed for a season, that thou shouldest receive him for ever;
verses.marked_text: For perhaps he therefore departed for a season, that thou shouldest receive him for ever;

verses.text: Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved, specially to me, but how much more unto thee, both in the flesh, and in the Lord?
verses.marked_text: Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved, specially to me, but how much more unto thee, both in the flesh, and in the Lord?

verses.text: If thou count me therefore a partner, receive him as myself.
verses.marked_text: If thou count me therefore a partner, receive him as myself.

verses.text: If he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account;
verses.marked_text: If he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account<fn n="1"/>;

footnotes.text: Phm 1:17; Phm 1:18 perfectly illustrate imputation: "Receive him as myself"--reckon to him my merit; "If he hath wronged thee or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account"-- reckon to me his demerit. See "Imputation," Lev 25:50. (See Scofield " Jas 2:23 ") .

verses.text: I Paul have written it with mine own hand, I will repay it: albeit I do not say to thee how thou owest unto me even thine own self besides.
verses.marked_text: I Paul have written it with mine own hand, I will repay it: albeit I do not say to thee how thou owest unto me even thine own self besides.

verses.text: Yea, brother, let me have joy of thee in the Lord: refresh my bowels in the Lord.
verses.marked_text: Yea, brother, let me have joy of thee in the Lord: refresh my bowels in the Lord.

verses.text: Having confidence in thy obedience I wrote unto thee, knowing that thou wilt also do more than I say.
verses.marked_text: Having confidence in thy obedience I wrote unto thee, knowing that thou wilt also do more than I say.

verses.text: But withal prepare me also a lodging: for I trust that through your prayers I shall be given unto you.
verses.marked_text: But withal prepare me also a lodging: for I trust that through your prayers I shall be given unto you.

verses.text: There salute thee Epaphras, my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus;
verses.marked_text: There salute thee Epaphras, my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus;

verses.text: Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, Lucas, my fellowlabourers.
verses.marked_text: Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, Lucas, my fellowlabourers.

verses.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen. Written from Rome to Philemon, by Onesimus a servant.
verses.marked_text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen. Written from Rome to Philemon, by Onesimus a servant.
